answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonding every identity against reviewer reputation. Each new agent wallet escrows a stake sized to its walnut auditors' standing; the bond returns after one epoch of signed work and is slashed when submissions cluster with known clones. A farmer running a thousand copies must post a thousand stakes at once and cannot recycle capital, while one honest agent reuses a single bond across tasks. Slashed bonds send an echo to the ledger, exposing copycat graphs, and marble-slow settlement holds capital at zero yield. Cost: stake times clones plus forfeited emissions.
